§3.2 Markdown Rendering

📚 Document rule — needs other pages of the document; decided once and applied on every page

output-markdown-rendering · output output-model markdown

✅ Normative

The output MUST be one Markdown document for the whole document, with pages in order separated by a line holding only ---, and each page's elements in reading order. Where Markdown has no syntax for a construct, the output MUST use the HTML element this protocol names, and MUST NOT invent a notation of its own.

Page boundaries

  • Pages MUST appear in document order, each separated from the next by a line containing only ---, preceded and followed by a blank line.
  • --- MUST NOT be used for anything else. A printed separator rule is <hr/> — see Line Separators and Breaks§6.3 — and printed text that begins with --- is escaped — see Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4.
  • A page with no ink at all is represented by the single line <!-- blank page --> — see Ignoring and Rejecting§5.6.
  • Content MUST stay on the page it is printed on: a table, paragraph or cell that runs onto the next page is split at the boundary — see Cross-Page Tables§4.3 and Output Options§3.5.

Markdown first, HTML where Markdown cannot

Construct Rendering
Headings ATX # headings
Bold / italic Markdown ** / *; inside HTML tables, see Bold and Italic Inside Tables§9.6.2
Underline, superscript, subscript, highlight <u>, <sup>, <sub>, <mark>
Meaningful text colour <font color="NAME">
Tables HTML <table> with <tr>, <th>, <td>, rowspan, colspan
Tables representing charts HTML <table data-source="chart"> — see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1
Table and chart captions <caption>…</caption> first or last inside <table> according to reading order — see Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3
Printed separator rule <hr/>
Line break inside one block a plain newline — see Line Breaks Inside a Block§6.2
Maths $$ … $$, inline and displayed
Diagrams and blueprints fenced diagram/<language> block; fenced description only when no suitable language can faithfully represent the content

Tables MUST be HTML because spanning cells, multi-tier headers and multi-line cells cannot be expressed in pipe tables; pipe tables MUST NOT be used. See Nested Tables§9.5.2.

Markers

The protocol defines a small set of bracketed markers for printed things that are not text. They are the only placeholders allowed: [blank] an empty field, [x] / [ ] a checkbox, [signature] / [signature:{name}], [seal: …], [logo: …] / [logo], [watermark: …], [stamp: …] / [stamp], [handwritten: …], [REDACTED]. Each is defined in its own rule.

Page header and footer bands

A header band MUST be rendered as its own paragraph(s) at the start of its page's content and a footer band at the end, never as a heading. A producer MAY wrap each band in <header>…</header> / <footer>…</footer>, so a consumer can drop or keep furniture without guessing where it ends; the wrapper is optional, and output with or without it conforms.
